issues.changes: Replaced the empty annular TIR1 aperture with an experimentally derived local binding site from 2P1Q. TIR1 chain B contact residues, IAC auxin and the modeled chain C IAA7 degron use one deposited-coordinate transform; bound ligand is contacted by receptor atoms and capped by degron atoms. Both languages distinguish the selected structural site from schematic SCF and motion.
verification: Actual transformed mesh triangles are queried with THREE.Triangle.closestPointToPoint, not nearest vertices. At p=.40 receptor–IAA minimum VDW surface gap is -0.01712 scene units and degron–IAA gap is +0.01300; multiple atoms must contact each partner and gross overlap fails.

Every displayed binding-site atom is compared against its deposited coordinate under the same assembly transform. Both auxin controls are covered by stage, finite geometry and deterministic-seek checks.
limitations: The displayed structural subset includes complete 19 TIR1 residues with any heavy atom within 6 Å of IAC (161 atoms), all 114 modeled IAA7 atoms and 13 IAC atoms; waters and IHP are omitted. It is a local structural site, not a reconstructed full TIR1 atomic model.
Outer SCF, full Aux/IAA and travel/unfolding are teaching schematics. Molecular movement is not an atomic simulation. Root visual acceptance remains pending.

issues.changes: The same four ubiquitin objects move from the tagging/substrate state to an intact released-chain recycling path. They are independent of the shrinking Aux/IAA group. The physical substrate–ubiquitin link is removed before substrate loss; no separate recycled copies remain.
verification: Samples p=.48–.80 retain exactly the original four ubiquitin UUIDs at fixed world radius .085 while substrate loss proceeds.
The attachment link is absent after p=.63, and the low-auxin control has no visible induced ubiquitin chain.
limitations: Four illustrated ubiquitins and the intact-chain recycling path summarize deubiquitination; chain disassembly/reuse kinetics and linkage chemistry are not simulated.

issues.changes: Added flexible cytosolic juxtamembrane links and mobile kinase lobes. FLS2–BAK1 contact precedes receptor phosphomarks; receptor-bound BIK1 is phosphorylated before release and docks against RBOHD before its phosphomarks appear.
verification: Raycaster triangle-surface interface gaps at first visible phosphomarks: FLS2–BAK1 p=.49 = -0.00198, FLS2–BIK1 p=.51 = -0.01643, BIK1–RBOHD p=.68 = -0.00246 scene units. Each must fall in the contact interval (-.06,.02).

Each phosphomark is absent immediately before its event; the no-flg22 control remains unphosphorylated. Both branches pass finite geometry, deterministic seeking, stable resource inventory and browser bundling.
limitations: Intracellular docking poses are mechanism schematics, not coordinates inferred from the ectodomain-only 4MN8 crystal. These tests establish depicted physical contact and activation order, not atomically resolved kinase chemistry.

issues.changes: Reduced the BAK1 lateral z detour to remain inside the displayed membrane. Lipid head/tail exclusion follows the current BAK1 footprint, refilling vacated positions instead of leaving permanent initial/final holes.
verification: Both control branches at 202 total progress samples satisfy transmembrane-span containment: absolute BAK1 z plus its .10 radius stays below the .61 displayed head boundary.
Actual paired leaflet instance transforms are checked: a lipid slot is collapsed only inside the current BAK1 footprint, and vacated slots are restored.
limitations: The membrane is a finite schematic bilayer patch and lipid displacement is illustrative, not molecular diffusion.

commands.result: PASS: four scientific regressions, both controls, finite buffers/bounds, deterministic seeks, stable object/resource inventory, and owned-module browser bundling.
